text:
The patient most likely has irritable bowel syndrome, and the sympathetic innervation of the colon originates from preganglionic neurons in the intermediolateral cell column (lateral horn) of the thoracolumbar spinal cord, about T10-L2. Midgut fibers reach the colon via the thoracic splanchnic nerves and superior mesenteric ganglion, and hindgut fibers via the lumbar splanchnic nerves and inferior mesenteric ganglion. The team note about lumbosacral origin is incorrect, because sacral segments (S2-S4) supply parasympathetic outflow, not sympathetic.

CONFIDENCE: 85
